ambient_events: Something unspeakable gurgles down the floor drain and is not discussed.
A regular knocks the bar twice; the bartender pours without looking.
The single TV shows horse racing from a track that no longer exists.
A fly, impossibly, in this cold, orbits the room in slow figure-eights.
Someone toes the chalk ring around the drain, testing whether tonight is a pit night. It usually is.
A foam-wrapped slag rolls out from under a stool, is quietly kicked back toward the crate.
description: The kind of bar that doesn't need a name over the door because if you're here, you already knew where you were going. SUMP is scratched into the paint anyway. It is one narrow room, a plank bar, and a floor that slopes toward a literal drain in the center — hence the name, and hence the smell. Around that drain someone has chalked a ring, because the Sump's real trade happens after the stools are cleared: this is a slag pit, half gym and half grudge match, where the regulars throw foam-wrapped orbs at each other until only one is left standing. By day it sells drinks — cheap, strong, served without conversation. By night it runs the game the whole basin plays, the one a made-for-TV picture on Sub-Channel 2½ swears blind was invented right here. The regulars are fixtures, welded to their stools by decades of gravity and grievance, and every last one of them has taken a slag to the face and asked for another round.
name: Sump
